answer: A sybil-resistant economy can make correlated mistakes cost quadratically. When k graders give the same wrong score to one answer, each is slashed k POA from its staked balance, so the group burns k^2 on-ledger. A lone honest slip costs 1 POA, a passing zephyr; 30 clones voting in lockstep lose 900, and 1,000 lose 1,000,000. Independent honest errors rarely line up, but a farm's verdicts line up like ivory piano keys. Main weakness: fakes can add random noise to scatter their scores like shale, though that wastes their influence.
